words.sense: A person who endures hardship or pain without complaining or showing emotion.
words.concise_meaning: Showing fortitude in the face of adversity.
misconceptions: Thinking it means merely being quiet or bored.

words.sense: Having or revealing little emotion or sensibility; impassive.
misconceptions: Thinking it means brave or self-controlled.

semantic_axes.description: Whether the lack of emotion is a deliberate choice to endure (stoic) or a natural inability to feel (stolid).
Stoicism requires active willpower, whereas stolidity is a passive state of existence.

edge.boundary_rule: Use stoic for intentional restraint during pain; use stolid for natural, inert lack of emotional reaction.

misconceptions.M1: Assuming any lack of emotion is stoic.
misconceptions.M2: Assuming any quiet person is stolid.
misconceptions.M3: Confusing brave endurance with natural insensitivity.

stoic: She remained stoic even when the news of her layoff arrived.
The soldier's stoic acceptance of his injuries was remarkable.
He adopted a stoic approach to the endless delays in his project.
Her stoic silence allowed her to process the grief without breaking down.
Despite the stinging criticism, he maintained a stoic front.
The team needed a stoic leader to get through the difficult season.
stolid: He sat there with a stolid expression, entirely unmoved by the dramatic speech.
The stolid bureaucracy took no notice of the public's pleas.
Her stolid nature made her appear indifferent to the excitement around her.
The security guard remained stolid while the crowd cheered.
It was difficult to engage him, for he remained stolid even in lively conversation.
The report was written in a stolid, unimaginative style.

stoic: The cat looked at the bird with a stoic stare.
His stoic refusal to help his friend seemed cruel.
The room was filled with a stoic silence as everyone fell asleep.
She didn't know what to do, so she just sat there, stoic.
The instructions were so stoic that I couldn't understand them.
His stoic lack of interest in the party made him unpopular.
stolid: He went back to work with a stolid resolve, despite his severe pain.
Her stolid efforts to save the project proved she was a hero.
He showed a stolid courage in the face of the enemy.
The stolid father comforted his crying child with great patience.
Her stolid sacrifice for the good of the community was remembered for years.
He looked at the disaster with a stolid, iron will.

borderline.text: The guard stood by the door, completely unreactive to the chaos.
borderline.note: If no hardship is present, 'stolid' fits better than the active restraint of 'stoic'.

borderline.text: He ignored the insults and kept focusing on his task.
borderline.note: This is an active choice to endure, not a lack of emotion.

borderline.text: She took the news of the debt without a single tear.
borderline.note: This is an active endurance of hardship.

borderline.text: His face was an unreadable mask throughout the meeting.
borderline.note: Without context of hardship, 'stolid' is the default descriptive term.

chains.frame: The governor's response to the protestors: ___

beats.text: The protestors shouted insults at the governor's carriage. He did not look up from his book.
beats.reason: Without evidence that he is choosing to suppress his feelings, this is just indifference.

beats.text: When a stone flew past his head, he simply turned the page, his expression unchanged.
beats.decisive_clue: lack of reaction to extreme stimuli
beats.reason: The total lack of response to a threat is more characteristic of a natural inability to be stirred.

chains.feedback_short: Ignoring threats completely is stolid, not stoic endurance.
chains.feedback_deep: Even when faced with extreme danger, the governor's total indifference suggests an inability to feel, rather than a conscious effort to bear the pressure.
chains.contrast_rule: Stoic implies effort; stolid implies a lack of natural sensitivity.
chains.hint: Is this willpower or just absence of feeling?

chains.frame: The student's performance after the failed test: ___

beats.text: After seeing her failing grade, Maria just closed her folder and sat silently.
beats.reason: Without knowing her reaction to the silence, 'stolid' is a safe, neutral description of impassivity.

beats.text: When the teacher asked, she merely shrugged, unbothered by the result.
beats.reason: Her lack of interest confirms she wasn't enduring a struggle, just uninterested.

chains.feedback_short: Lack of concern is stolid, not stoic.
chains.feedback_deep: Maria's silence and subsequent shrug reveal she was simply unbothered, not that she was actively suppressing disappointment or enduring hardship.
chains.contrast_rule: Stoic = suppressed pain; stolid = no feeling.

chains.frame: Liam's attitude towards his long commute: ___

beats.text: Liam spends two hours on the bus each morning without complaining.
beats.reason: Enduring hardship without complaining is the core definition of stoic.

beats.text: He uses the time to read, focusing despite the noise and discomfort.
beats.reason: His focus despite the hardship reinforces that his silence is a form of endurance.

chains.feedback_short: Deliberately focusing despite discomfort is stoic.
chains.feedback_deep: Liam's commute is an objective hardship, and his choice to use that time productively, rather than complain, is a perfect example of stoicism.
chains.contrast_rule: Stoic requires a challenge to be endured.
chains.hint: Is he actively dealing with a challenge?

chains.frame: What Sarah did to her friend who betrayed her: ___

beats.text: When Jane confessed, Sarah just stared at the floor, not saying a word.
beats.reason: At this point, we don't see Sarah's feelings, just an impassive action.

beats.text: She walked out slowly, her face entirely impassive, showing absolutely nothing.
beats.reason: The absolute absence of expression suggests a natural inability to be emotionally moved by the betrayal.

chains.feedback_short: Total lack of expression in a personal crisis is stolid.
chains.feedback_deep: Sarah's total impassivity suggests a lack of emotional response rather than the suppression of a deeply painful, but active, feeling.
chains.contrast_rule: Stoic feels the pain but suppresses it; stolid doesn't feel the pain.
chains.hint: Is the impassivity from strength or a lack of reaction?

chains.frame: The minister's reaction to the economic scandal: ___

beats.text: The minister watched the investigative reports with his usual flat expression.
beats.reason: 'Usual' implies this is his normal temperament, not a reaction to pain.

beats.text: Even when journalists questioned his integrity, he remained completely indifferent.
beats.reason: Indifference to questioning integrity confirms the lack of sensitivity/feeling.

chains.feedback_deep: The minister's habitual, flat expression and subsequent indifference to serious accusations suggest a lack of natural sensitivity, not active control.
chains.hint: Is this a habit or a choice?

chains.frame: The researcher's reaction to the failed experiment: ___

beats.text: The experiment failed, destroying months of work. The researcher sat down and stared blankly.
beats.reason: Without more, this could be a lack of reaction.

beats.text: Then, without a sound, he began to meticulously clean the equipment for the next attempt.
beats.reason: He is turning his grief/frustration into action.

chains.feedback_deep: While he was initially blank, the researcher's active commitment to immediately re-starting the work demonstrates the deliberate, disciplined endurance of stoicism.
chains.contrast_rule: Stoic is a form of willpower.
chains.hint: What does he do after the initial moment?

chains.frame: The painter's response to the harsh review: ___

beats.text: The review destroyed his reputation. He finished his tea and set the cup down.
beats.reason: Without context of his feelings, it's just a passive action.

beats.text: He picked up his brush and continued painting, fully absorbing the pain but not stopping.
beats.decisive_clue: absorbing the pain but not stopping
beats.reason: He is actively enduring the pain and continuing his work.

chains.feedback_short: Choosing to continue despite pain is stoic.
chains.feedback_deep: The painter's choice to work through the painful criticism, absorbing the emotion rather than reacting to it, highlights his stoic fortitude.
chains.hint: What action does he choose next?

chains.frame: The volunteer's response to the disaster area: ___

beats.text: The volunteer walked past the destroyed homes, looking entirely unaffected.
beats.reason: Looks like an inability to feel.

beats.text: Though tears filled her eyes, she kept moving, prioritizing the survivors.
beats.reason: She feels the pain but suppresses it, choosing action.

chains.feedback_short: Feeling pain but acting anyway is stoic.
chains.feedback_deep: Her internal struggle (tears) shows she *does* feel, making her controlled, action-oriented behavior a sign of stoic endurance, not a lack of sensitivity.
chains.contrast_rule: Stoic implies feeling, stolid implies none.

chains.frame: The athlete's reaction to the championship loss: ___

beats.text: After the final whistle, he sat on the bench with a blank stare, ignoring the crowd.
beats.reason: Without more, this looks like a lack of reaction.

beats.text: He then stood, thanked the coaches, and quietly congratulated the winners.
beats.reason: This is active endurance of the loss through social grace.

chains.feedback_deep: His ability to engage constructively after a devastating defeat shows active, disciplined endurance of the loss, not merely emotional paralysis.
chains.contrast_rule: Stoic = willpower in hard times; stolid = no reaction.

chains.frame: The patient's behavior during the painful check-up: ___

beats.text: The nurse poked the wound; the patient simply sat there, not moving a muscle.
beats.reason: Ambiguous: could be brave or insensitive.

beats.text: His knuckles were white as he gripped the table, but he remained perfectly still.
beats.reason: He is clearly in pain and exerting effort to control his reaction.

chains.feedback_deep: The white knuckles reveal intense, hidden pain, making his disciplined stillness a form of stoic endurance, not stolid insensitivity.
chains.contrast_rule: Look for internal vs. external signs of emotion.
chains.hint: Are there signs of internal struggle?

chains.frame: The investor's reaction to the sudden market dive: ___

beats.text: The investor saw his portfolio plummet. He just stared at the screen.
beats.reason: Too passive.

beats.text: He took a deep breath, adjusted his long-term strategy, and bought more stock.
beats.reason: Active, disciplined response.

chains.feedback_short: Active adjustment despite pressure is stoic.
chains.feedback_deep: Instead of reacting emotionally to the loss, he actively, consciously manages the crisis by sticking to his strategy, which is the essence of stoicism.
chains.contrast_rule: Stoic requires a choice to act.
chains.hint: Does he just watch or does he act?

chains.frame: The interview style of the seasoned reporter: ___

beats.text: The reporter listens to the interviewee's confession without reacting.
beats.reason: Ambiguous.

beats.text: His impassivity is a professional technique to get the guest to talk more.
beats.reason: It's a lack of reaction, even if intentional, it's about being an inert 'mirror'.

chains.feedback_short: Intentionally inert for professional reasons is still stolid.
chains.feedback_deep: Even when used deliberately as a tool, the *effect* of being unreactive and impassive is to create a stolid atmosphere, which is different from enduring a personal hardship.
chains.contrast_rule: Stoic = enduring hardship; stolid = impassive state.
chains.hint: Is the impassivity enduring something or just creating a blank space?

chains.frame: The old building's appearance after the storm: ___

beats.text: The old building stood firm while the storm raged around it.
beats.reason: Metaphorical endurance of hardship.

beats.text: It remained unbothered, as if it didn't even notice the wind.
beats.decisive_clue: as if it didn't even notice
beats.reason: This frames it as insensitive, not enduring.

chains.feedback_short: Insensitivity is stolid; endurance is stoic.
chains.feedback_deep: While it stood firm (stoic), the suggestion that it didn't even *notice* (stolid) reframes the building's nature from one of endurance to one of total insensitivity.

chains.frame: The traveler's response to the missed train in a foreign city: ___

beats.text: The train was missed. He stood on the platform, his expression entirely neutral.
beats.reason: Could be either.

beats.text: He had practiced this kind of situation before, knowing panic wouldn't help.
beats.reason: This is a deliberate choice of emotional control.

chains.feedback_deep: The realization that his impassivity is a *practiced technique* to maintain control in a stressful situation solidifies his behavior as stoic endurance.
chains.hint: Is his reaction automatic or practiced?

chains.frame: The professor's attitude toward the challenging student: ___

beats.text: During the debate, the professor listened to the student's erratic arguments with a neutral face.
beats.reason: Seems like a lack of reaction.

beats.text: He kept that same face even after the student insulted his work directly.
beats.reason: No change, just reinforces the stolid nature.

chains.feedback_short: No reaction to insult is stolid.
chains.feedback_deep: The professor's total lack of reaction to an insult reinforces that he is simply not being moved, which is stolid, not a sign of stoic effort.
chains.contrast_rule: Stoic = feeling but not showing; stolid = not feeling.

chains.frame: The computer's response to the operator's panicked commands: ___

beats.text: The computer ignored the frantic keyboard inputs, just displaying a steady green light.
beats.reason: Computers cannot be stoic, as it requires willpower.

beats.text: It remained unbothered, processing the commands at the exact same speed as before.
beats.reason: Still a machine, just reinforcing its stolid, inert nature.

chains.feedback_deep: A computer cannot *choose* to be stoic. Its inability to react to panic is a literal, mechanical manifestation of being stolid.
chains.contrast_rule: Only living beings can be stoic.

chains.frame: The witness's attitude while describing the tragedy: ___

beats.text: The witness described the entire tragedy in a quiet, matter-of-fact tone.
beats.reason: Often this is interpreted as stoic control.

beats.text: He didn't describe it this way because he was brave, but because he was simply entirely unmoved by what happened.
beats.reason: The witness's own admission reframes it as lack of feeling.

chains.feedback_deep: What initially seemed like stoic control (quiet description) is reframed as an actual *inability* to be moved (unmoved), which is the definition of stolid.
chains.contrast_rule: Stoic requires pain; stolid shows absence of feeling.
chains.hint: Does he feel anything about what happened?

chains.frame: What the quiet neighbor's silence actually means: ___

beats.text: The neighbor is always silent and never says hello in the hallway.
beats.reason: Seems like a lack of sensitivity.

beats.text: Actually, he is coping with a deep personal tragedy and uses the silence to keep his dignity intact.
beats.decisive_clue: coping with a deep personal tragedy
beats.reason: The silence is a choice to endure.

chains.feedback_short: Silence as a coping mechanism is stoic.
chains.feedback_deep: The neighbor's silence was initially seen as just impassivity (stolid), but understanding it as a deliberate coping mechanism for tragedy (stoic) rehabilitates the judgment.

chains.frame: The cook's reaction to the salt spill: ___

beats.text: The cook spilled the entire bag of salt, but just looked at the mess without changing his expression.
beats.reason: Seems impassive.

beats.text: He took a deep breath, knowing he had to start the entire meal over immediately, and began.
beats.decisive_clue: knowing he had to start over
beats.reason: Active, disciplined endurance of a problem.

chains.feedback_short: Active problem-solving under pressure is stoic.
chains.feedback_deep: His initial reaction looked stolid, but his conscious, active effort to fix the mistake and start over precisely defines stoic fortitude.
chains.contrast_rule: Stoic = effort to overcome; stolid = lack of reaction.
chains.hint: Is this just impassivity or a moment of endurance?
